recommendation: Keep the empty audit commit as-is for FHIR-31796. If the work group wants to polish the phrase "as whole" or otherwise improve the later package-content wording, handle that as a separate editorial issue.
issue_request: FHIR-31796 was a Published/Persuasive BR&R change request for FHIR-core-MedicinalProductPackaged asking to improve the weak PackagedProductDefinition.identifier definition for R5. The applied Jira comment says the element should identify the package as a whole and list unique instance identifiers assigned by manufacturers, regulators, drug catalogue custodians, or other organizations.
initial_application: Git commit 8f276af0294e5a576ebd983b58659aa54899dff2 explicitly cited FHIR#31796 and changed PackagedProductDefinition.identifier from generic "Unique identifier" text to the Jira-comment wording. Commit c58270261982846561c4e2c2a7612e2b1f660b55 synchronized the same wording from R4B.
additional_context: PackagedProductDefinition is active in the current build through source/fhir.ini. Related issue FHIR-31795 was implemented in the same first commit and explains the distinction between the whole-package identifier and packaging-part identifiers. Later issue FHIR-29783 added the current "not for the content of the package" clarification and was resolved No Change because the wording had already been updated.
reconciliation: No source change was made. The active StructureDefinition already says PackagedProductDefinition.identifier identifies the package as a whole, not the package contents, and includes the assigning-organization guidance requested by the seed issue. The remaining awkward grammar is editorial and does not create a semantic defect requiring a FHIR-31796 source-changing reconciliation.

related_jiras.note: Implemented in the same 2022 commit and explains the distinction between whole-package and package-part identifiers.
A later broader wording proposal added the current package-content clarification and was resolved No Change because the wording had already been updated.
